source.author: cic
source.text: in quo si te multum natura adiuvaret, si optimis a pueritia disciplinis atque artibus studuisses et in his elaborasses, si litteras Graecas Athenis non Lilybaei, Latinas Romae non in Sicilia didicisses, tamen esset magnum tantam causam, tam exspectatam, et diligentia consequi et memoria complecti et oratione expromere et voce ac viribus sustinere.
source.text_original: in quo si te multum natura adiuvaret, si optimis a pueritia disciplinis atque artibus studuisses et in his elaborasses, si litteras Graecas Athenis non Lilybaei, Latinas Romae non in Sicilia didicisses, tamen esset magnum tantam causam, tam exspectatam, et diligentia consequi et memoria complecti et oratione expromere et voce ac viribus sustinere.
source.text_english: in which, even if nature had helped you a great deal, if from childhood you had devoted yourself to the best studies and pursuits and had labored in them, if you had learned Greek letters at Athens and not at Lilybaeum, Latin at Rome and not in Sicily, still it would be a great thing to handle so important a case, so eagerly awaited, to grasp it with diligence, express it in speech, and sustain it with voice and strength.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: certe, si etiam praeclarus orator reprehendendum nescio quem putat, quod litteras Graecas non Athenis, sed Lilybaei, Latinas non Romae, sed in Sicilia didicerit, quod uidelicet unaquaeque prouincia habeat aliquid proprium, quod alia aeque habere non possit, cur nos putamus absque Athenis nostris quemquam ad studiorum fastigium peruenisse?
reuse.text_original: certe, si etiam praeclarus orator reprehendendum nescio quem putat, quod litteras Graecas non Athenis, sed Lilybaei, Latinas non Romae, sed in Sicilia didicerit, quod uidelicet unaquaeque prouincia habeat aliquid proprium, quod alia aeque habere non possit, cur nos putamus absque Athenis nostris quemquam ad studiorum fastigium peruenisse?
reuse.text_english: Certainly, if even a distinguished orator thinks someone ought to be criticized because he learned Greek letters not at Athens but at Lilybaeum, Latin not at Rome but in Sicily, since each province evidently has something peculiar that another cannot equally have, why do we think that anyone has reached the summit of learning without our own Athens?
